K=1 target-axis recovery and downstream interpretation. The AML-shaped synthetic longitudinal
calibration experiment to assess the declared condition target contrasts disease with control.
Red arrows mark the planted reference axis and black arrows show an abstract unsigned angle
reconstructed from absolute loading cosine in a schematic two-dimensional plane; panel A shows
successful geometric recovery with downstream interpretation not estimable; panel B shows
cosine agreement below the recovery threshold, with downstream interpretation not evaluated;
the upward orientation is illustrative, not an observed coordinate. The analysis unit is
complete synthetic mouse trajectory; the estimand is agreement between the planted and
recovered target axes, followed by estimability of the declared downstream interpretation; time
is recorded as collection time in weeks; adjustment uses batch. Only completed replicates with
evaluable recovery geometry are drawn in the component plane; execution failures and replicates
with unavailable recovery evidence or component-identity mismatch remain in the typed outcome
table and are not converted into geometric arrows. Axis recovery uses one canonical rule:
loading cosine at least 0.9; its equivalent angle is descriptive. These known-truth synthetic
results describe recovery under the tested settings only; they do not establish performance for
biological data. The displayed examples were selected explicitly by task ID: outcome-1,
outcome-3.
